body.text: Waste Reduction Measures
Reuse and Recovery

Dawar Group implements material reuse and recovery practices to minimize internal waste. Large leather scraps are repurposed into accessories such as wallets, belts, or keychains. Small fabric bits are reused as stuffing or cleaning cloths. Defective products are repurposed or repaired wherever possible, reducing waste in the production line.
Reduction of internal wastes through material reuse, recovery, or repurpose

Dawar Group actively reduces internal waste by repairing and reusing damaged or outdated equipment, repurposing furniture parts, and utilizing worn-out components in other production areas. For instance, damaged leather machinery covers are repurposed as protective padding, while worn-out tables and workstations are repaired rather than replaced. This approach has led to significant reductions in purchasing new materials and contributes to the company's sustainability goals.
Waste Sorting:
Waste will be sorted at the source to facilitate easier disposal and recycling. The sorting process will follow the classification below:

Non-Hazardous Waste (e.g., leather scraps, packaging materials, fabric bits) will be separated from hazardous waste and sent to local recycling plants or repurposed within the company.
Hazardous Waste (e.g., adhesives, chemicals) will be stored in containment units until they can be safely collected by certified waste management services.
Mixed Waste (e.g., combined material items like shoes with both leather and metal components) will be disassembled before disposal, and each material will be sorted accordingly.
Employee Training:

All employees will undergo annual training on waste minimization techniques, including the correct methods for sorting and handling both hazardous and non-hazardous materials. This will ensure that waste is sorted efficiently, minimizing contamination of recyclable materials
Evidence of Compliance
Regular Monitoring and Evaluation

Waste Management Records: All waste disposal activities will be recorded and audited regularly. Detailed logs will be maintained for hazardous waste, including adhesive containers and chemical solvents. Records will also include evidence of reused materials, such as repurposed leather scraps and repaired machinery components.
Inspection Reports: Regular inspections will be carried out by the Environmental Manager to ensure compliance with waste disposal guidelines. These reports will also track the repair and reuse of equipment and repurposed materials as evidence of the company's commitment to waste reduction.
Training Records: A log of all employee training sessions on waste management, including sorting and disposal practices, will be kept by the HR Department.

Ensures that defective products are either recycled, reused, or donated, and tracks the disposal of materials that cannot be repurposed.

sops.title: Workplace Safety Incident & Risk Management System

blocks.text: This SOP outlines the procedures for identifying, reporting, and managing workplace safety incidents, risks, and concerns at Dawar Group. The aim is to ensure a safe working environment for all employees by minimizing hazards and promoting a culture of safety awareness, especially in the handcrafted footwear production environment.

This SOP applies to all employees, contractors, and visitors at Dawar Group across all production facilities. It covers procedures for reporting and addressing safety incidents, conducting risk assessments, and implementing corrective actions. Special emphasis is placed on the manual handling of tools and materials, exposure to adhesives, and the use of sharp cutting tools.

rows: 12.5 Km Near Bapu Asaram Ashram, Agra Delhi Road, Sikandra 282007 Agra, Uttar Pradesh India.

body.text: Employees must report any workplace safety incident or near-miss to their supervisor immediately. Examples include injuries from cutting tools, chemical exposure, slips, or equipment malfunctions.

The supervisor will document the incident using the Workplace Safety Incident Report Form, including details such as the date, time, location, persons involved, and a brief description of the incident.
The supervisor will take immediate steps to secure the area and prevent further incidents. This may include cordoning off the area, providing first aid, or shutting down equipment.
Annual risk assessments must be conducted in all work areas to identify potential hazards, particularly those related to manual shoe production, leather handling, stitching, and adhesives use.
All identified risks must be recorded in a Risk Register, with details on the nature of the risk, the likelihood of occurrence, potential impact, and control measures in place.
Appropriate control measures must be implemented to mitigate identified risks. This can include engineering controls, administrative controls, and personal protective equipment (PPE).
A team comprising members of the Safety Committee and relevant supervisors will investigate all reported incidents.
The investigation team will conduct a root cause analysis to identify underlying causes and contributing factors to the incident.
Based on the findings, the team will recommend CAPAs to prevent recurrence. The implementation of these actions will be tracked and documented.

blocks.text: All employees must undergo safety training during onboarding and receive regular refresher courses. Topics covered will include hazard identification, safe work practices, and emergency response procedures, with a focus on handling cutting tools, chemicals, and adhesives.

responsibilities: Report any safety incidents or concerns immediately to the supervisor or Safety Officer.

Maintain incident and training records.

Provide resources and support for safety initiatives.

blocks.text: This SOP will be reviewed by the Health and Safety Manager every two years or following any significant incident to ensure its continued relevance and effectiveness in maintaining workplace safety standards.

sops.title: Hazardous Waste Management and Disposal Procedure

blocks.text: This SOP outlines the procedures for the safe handling, storage, and disposal of hazardous waste generated during Dawar Group’s operations, ensuring compliance with local environmental regulations and minimizing health and environmental risks. The focus is on minimizing material consumption, adopting eco-friendly materials, and reducing hazardous substances by using greener alternatives. Dawar Group is also committed to the safe disposal of hazardous waste to reduce environmental impact.

This procedure applies to all employees and contractors involved in the handling, storage, and disposal of hazardous waste and materials at Dawar Group’s facilities. It includes processes for material reduction through optimization, use of eco-friendly materials, and alternative substances. It also outlines the safe handling and disposal of hazardous waste.

rows: 12.5 Km Near Bapu Asaram Ashram, Agra Delhi Road, Sikandra 282007 Agra, Uttar Pradesh India.

body.text: Hazardous waste at Dawar Group includes, but is not limited to:

Adhesives and Solvents: Used in footwear assembly and finishing processes.
Chemical Waste: Such as dyeing agents, cleaning chemicals, and polishing substances.
Used Oils and Lubricants: Generated from machinery maintenance.
Expired Cleaning Agents: Containing toxic or flammable components.
Contaminated PPE: Personal protective equipment that has come into contact with hazardous materials.
Empty Chemical Containers: Including cans, drums, or bottles that contained hazardous chemicals

Identification: All employees are responsible for identifying hazardous waste generated in their work area. Hazardous waste labels must be applied to all containers holding such materials. Labels must include the type of waste, date, and department to ensure proper handling and disposal.
Segregation: Hazardous waste must be segregated according to its type (flammable, corrosive, toxic, reactive) and must not be mixed with non-hazardous waste. Waste segregation helps prevent dangerous chemical reactions and ensures compliance with waste management regulations.

sections.title: Reduction of Material Consumption through Process Optimization

steps.heading: Reduction of Material Consumption through Process Optimization

body.text:
Material Optimization:

Dawar Group adopts technologies and processes to minimize material consumption during production. For example, cutting processes are optimized to maximize material use and minimize waste. The company also uses efficient dyeing techniques that require fewer auxiliary chemicals, reducing chemical consumption and waste.

Examples of Reduction Measures:

Optimized Cutting Techniques: Advanced software is used in pattern cutting to maximize material use and reduce off-cuts.
Dyeing Efficiency: Dawar Group employs low-liquor-ratio dyeing techniques, reducing the water, energy, and chemicals required in the process.

Use of Recovered Input Materials

Reuse and Recovery:

Dawar Group recovers input materials for reuse and repurposes them in other applications. This includes the recovery of furniture parts, equipment components, and repairing or repurposing used materials. These recovered materials are reintroduced into the production process to reduce raw material consumption.

Examples of Recovery Measures:

Furniture and Equipment: Damaged or worn-out furniture and equipment parts are repaired and reused in production areas, reducing the need for new purchases.
Repurposing Material Waste: Leather off-cuts are repurposed into smaller accessories or product components to reduce waste.

Use of Eco-friendly or Bio-based Input Materials

Eco-friendly Materials:

Dawar Group uses biodegradable and eco-friendly input materials to reduce the environmental impact of its operations. Plant-based materials, biodegradable plastics, and natural dyes are incorporated into production to minimize hazardous waste generation and reduce the overall environmental footprint.

Examples of Eco-friendly Measures:

Biodegradable Plastics: Used in packaging and product components to ensure they break down naturally in the environment.
Plant-based Natural Dyes: Dawar Group uses vegetation-based natural dyes, which are non-toxic and safer for the environment compared to synthetic dyes.

Labeling, Storing, Handling, and Transporting Hazardous Substances

Hazardous Substances Protocols:

Dawar Group implements specific protocols to label, store, handle, and transport hazardous substances. All hazardous materials are labeled with clear hazard symbols and detailed descriptions of the contents to prevent mishandling. Approved containers are used for storing these substances in designated storage areas that are well-ventilated and isolated from flammable materials.

Handling and Transport Procedures:

Employees handling hazardous substances must wear appropriate PPE and follow the company’s protocols for safe handling. Hazardous waste is transported in sealed, approved containers to certified disposal facilities.

Specialized Treatment and Safe Disposal of Hazardous Substances

Specialized Disposal Protocols:

Dawar Group ensures that hazardous waste undergoes specialized treatment to minimize environmental impact. All hazardous substances are processed at certified facilities capable of neutralizing toxic components before disposal. The company also ensures that all waste is documented and tracked throughout its disposal journey to ensure compliance with environmental regulations.

Examples of Specialized Disposal Measures:

Chemical Neutralization: Hazardous chemicals are sent to licensed facilities where they are neutralized and treated to remove harmful elements before final disposal.
Documentation: Every hazardous waste disposal is tracked with a Waste Transfer Form, ensuring transparency and compliance.

Use of Alternative, Less Hazardous Substances in Operations

Substituting Harmful Chemicals:

Dawar Group is committed to reducing the use of harmful chemicals in operations by adopting alternative, less hazardous substances. For example, enzyme-based processes are used in place of chemical softeners, and biodegradable surfactants are introduced in place of traditional solvents. These substitutions reduce the risk of environmental contamination and improve the safety of handling materials.

Examples of Greener Alternatives:

Biodegradable Surfactants: Used in cleaning and finishing processes to replace traditional, toxic solvents.
Enzyme-based Bio-processing: Replaces chemical softeners and bleaching agents in the dyeing process.
Natural Plant Dyes: Used in place of synthetic dyes to ensure that dyes used in production are eco-friendly and safe for disposal.

sops.title: Sustainable Product Lifecycle Management and Packaging Optimization SOP

blocks.text: This SOP outlines Dawar Group’s commitment to sustainable product lifecycle management, including product recovery, packaging optimization, and environmentally responsible disposal practices. The focus is on minimizing environmental impact by adopting circular economy principles, which encourage the reuse, remanufacturing, and recycling of materials. Dawar Group is also committed to using eco-friendly packaging materials and reducing waste generation during product manufacturing and distribution.

This SOP applies to all Dawar Group products and involves collaboration with customers, suppliers, and local communities to ensure products are properly recycled or repurposed at the end of their lifecycle. It covers primary packaging optimization, product design for easy disassembly and recycling, and customer engagement in take-back programs.

sections.title: Information on Proper Disposal of Products to Promote Circular Material Flow

body.text: Dawar Group provides detailed instructions on how to return, recycle, or dispose of products at the end of their lifecycle. These instructions are included with each product and available on the company’s website. Customers are informed about local collection points, recycling facilities, and sanitary waste management options to ensure that products and materials remain in circulation and out of landfills. Visit the website at www.dawarfootwear.com/recycling.

By emphasizing product returns for remanufacturing or recycling, Dawar Group ensures that materials such as leather, textiles, and packaging are reused, reducing the need for virgin resources. The company encourages the use of biodegradable materials to further reduce environmental impact and ensure that waste is kept to a minimum.

sections.title: Optimization of Primary Packaging to Reduce Dimensions, Weight, or Simplify Material Mix

body.text: Dawar Group has implemented lightweight packaging designs to minimize material use while ensuring the protection of products during shipment. Monomaterial packaging (e.g., 100% recycled cardboard or biodegradable plastics) is prioritized to make recycling easier for consumers. Secondary packaging (e.g., shrink wrap) is eliminated to reduce waste.

By reducing the complexity of materials used in packaging, Dawar Group ensures that the entire packaging can be easily recycled. Water-based adhesives and recyclable labels are used to simplify the disposal process and ensure that packaging can be processed efficiently at recycling facilities.

sections.title: Design for Easy Disassembling, Remanufacturing, or Recycling

body.text: Dawar Group designs its products to enable easy disassembly and recycling. Modular designs and snap-fit components are used instead of glue or proprietary fasteners, making it simpler to separate materials for recycling or remanufacturing. This approach helps to reduce landfill waste and ensures materials can be repurposed for new products.

Returned products are assessed for remanufacturing or recycling. Materials such as leather, metal parts, and textiles are repurposed or sent to certified recycling partners for processing into new raw materials.

sections.title: Take-back or Buy-back Program to Collect Products for Remanufacture, Recycling, or Safe Disposal

These returned products are processed for remanufacturing, recycling, or safe disposal through certified recycling partners.

To encourage greater participation, Dawar Group offers store credits or discounts on future purchases when customers return their used products. This initiative promotes circular economy practices, ensuring that valuable materials are recycled and reused.

sops.title: IT Security Incident Handling & Recovery Procedure

blocks.text: This SOP establishes the procedures for identifying, responding to, and recovering from IT security incidents at Dawar Group. The primary goal is to ensure that security threats are managed swiftly to minimize the impact on operations, protect sensitive information, and restore normal IT services as soon as possible. This aligns with Dawar Group's Information Security Management System (ISMS) to proactively safeguard data and assets.

This SOP applies to all employees, IT staff, contractors, and third-party service providers at Dawar Group. It covers incidents such as data breaches, malware attacks, unauthorized access, system outages, phishing attempts, and any other cybersecurity threats that may compromise IT systems and data. The SOP is part of the overall framework established by Dawar Group’s IT Security Policy, forming a critical aspect of ISMS.

rows: 12.5 Km Near Bapu Asaram Ashram, Agra Delhi Road, Sikandra 282007 Agra, Uttar Pradesh India.

blocks.text: Security incidents at Dawar Group may include, but are not limited to:

Data Breaches: Unauthorized access to sensitive or confidential data, including personally identifiable information (PII).
Malware and Ransomware: Malicious software designed to damage, disrupt, or gain unauthorized access to systems.
Phishing Attacks: Attempts to steal sensitive information through deceptive emails or websites.
Denial-of-Service (DoS) Attacks: Efforts to overwhelm network services, making them unavailable to users.
Unauthorized Access: Any incident where an individual gains access to systems or data without proper authorization.
Insider Threats: Security risks originating from within the organization, including employees or contractors misusing their access.
System Outages: Any IT service interruption that could compromise security, including server crashes or network outages.

narrative.text:
Incident Detection:

All employees must be vigilant for signs of IT security incidents, such as unexpected system behavior, unauthorized access, or phishing emails. Dawar Group’s IT security monitoring systems will continuously monitor network activity to detect and flag suspicious activity. These systems follow the principles outlined in the ISMS, including logging and monitoring key security events.

Reporting Procedures:

Employees must immediately report any suspected or confirmed security incidents to the IT Helpdesk or IT Security Team. Reporting can be done through email, phone, or using a dedicated Incident Reporting Form. This aligns with the ISMS's requirement for prompt reporting and response to security threats.

Reporting Channels:

Email: security@dawarfootwear.com
Phone: +91 8865053163
Incident Form: Available on Dawar Group’s intranet.

blocks.text: Once an incident is reported, the following response steps are initiated:

body.text: The IT Security Team will assess the nature and severity of the incident, categorizing it as low, medium, or high severity based on the impact and urgency. This initial assessment follows the ISMS vulnerability management protocols, ensuring that identified weaknesses are addressed promptly.
If the incident is confirmed, the team will take immediate steps to contain the threat and prevent it from spreading. This could involve:

Isolating affected systems from the network.
Disabling compromised accounts.
Blocking malicious IP addresses or domains.
Once the incident is contained, efforts are focused on removing the threat from the affected systems. This involves:

Scanning systems for malware or unauthorized software.
Removing compromised files or malicious code.
Patching vulnerabilities that allowed the attack.
After eradication, the focus shifts to restoring systems to normal operation:

Restoring from backups (if necessary).
Rebuilding affected systems or servers.
Testing systems to ensure the threat has been fully eradicated.
The data backup processes in the ISMS ensure that critical data can be restored securely.

Once the incident has been resolved, the IT Security Team will conduct a root cause analysis to determine how the incident occurred and to identify areas for improvement. A detailed Incident Report will be compiled, outlining the incident, response actions, and recovery efforts. This is in line with the security incident management guidelines under the ISMS.

blocks.text:
Clear communication is essential during an IT security incident. The IT Security Team will coordinate communication with affected stakeholders, including:

Internal Communication:

The IT Security Team will inform affected employees, department heads, and senior management about the status of the incident. Updates will be provided regularly until the issue is resolved.

External Communication:

If the incident involves external parties (e.g., vendors, partners, or customers), the Public Relations and Legal Teams will work together to manage communication, ensuring transparency while protecting the company’s reputation and complying with legal obligations
All IT security incidents must be documented in detail. The Incident Report should include the following information

Incident Summary: A brief description of the incident, including how it was detected and reported.
Timeline: Key dates and times for incident detection, containment, and resolution.
Impact Assessment: Details on the impact of the incident, including affected systems, data, and services.
Actions Taken: A step-by-step overview of containment, eradication, and recovery efforts.
Root Cause Analysis: Findings from the post-incident analysis, identifying vulnerabilities or weaknesses that led to the incident.
Lessons Learned: Recommendations to prevent similar incidents in the future.
This documentation aligns with the ISMS, which mandates security incident management to be thoroughly documented and reviewed.

responsibilities: Primary responsibility for incident detection, response, containment, and recovery. The team is tasked with monitoring systems for threats, managing security tools, and implementing security protocols. During an incident, they lead the triage, containment, and recovery efforts, ensuring alignment with the ISMS guidelines.

Work with the IT Security Team to isolate affected systems, apply patches, and assist in restoring systems to normal operations. They are also responsible for ensuring that backups are current and available for recovery, as specified in the data backup procedures of the ISMS.

Acts as the main point of contact during a security incident. Responsible for coordinating communication between different teams (IT, Legal, Public Relations) and ensuring that the response follows the SOP.

Responsible for promptly reporting any suspicious activity or potential security threats. Employees must adhere to the ISMS policies, including user access management, acceptable use policies, and participate in mandatory cybersecurity training. They are expected to avoid suspicious links, use strong passwords, and comply with all company security protocols.

Ensures that appropriate resources are allocated for the IT security team and that regular security audits and risk assessments are conducted. Management is also responsible for supporting annual ISMS reviews to ensure compliance with security standards.

blocks.text: Once the security incident has been contained and eradicated, the IT Security Team will work with System Administrators to restore systems and ensure the return to normal operations. This involves:

Restoring from Backups: In case data was compromised, encrypted, or lost, backups will be used to recover critical information and restore systems. Backup protocols are in line with the ISMS Data Backup Policy.
Testing Restored Systems: All restored systems and applications will be tested for functionality and to confirm that the security threat has been completely removed.
Business Continuity: Dawar Group’s Business Continuity Plan (BCP) will be activated if the incident affects critical systems that disrupt business operations for an extended period.

Incident Response Drills:

The IT Security Team will conduct regular incident response drills to simulate various security incidents, ensuring that the team is prepared to handle real-world threats efficiently.

This SOP will be reviewed every two years by the IT Security Team. The review will evaluate the effectiveness of incident response protocols, compliance with regulatory standards, and alignment with best practices in cybersecurity. The team will assess recent security incidents for lessons learned and identify areas for improvement in threat detection and recovery processes. Any updates will be documented, and training will be provided to ensure employee awareness of the changes

sops.title: Authorization & Approval Process for Critical Transactions

blocks.text: This SOP outlines the procedure for the approval of sensitive transactions, including gifts, travel expenses, and other critical financial activities, to ensure compliance with company policies, ethical standards, and regulatory requirements. The goal is to prevent conflicts of interest, ensure transparency, and uphold the integrity of Dawar Group.
This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, and third parties who are involved in or responsible for initiating, approving, or processing sensitive transactions at Dawar Group.

rows: 12.5 Km Near Bapu Asaram Ashram, Agra Delhi Road, Sikandra 282007 Agra, Uttar Pradesh India.

rows.definition: Transactions involving gifts, travel, or other benefits that may create a conflict of interest or influence business decisions.
Designated individuals or departments responsible for reviewing and approving sensitive transactions.

body.text: All sensitive transactions must be identified and documented. Examples include gifts exceeding a specified monetary threshold, business travel for non-routine purposes, or other benefits. Thresholds: Gifts or benefits valued above ₹5,000 and travel expenses above ₹25,000 require specific approval.
Complete a Sensitive Transaction Request Form for each transaction. This form should include:

Name of the recipient
Description of the transaction (gift, travel, etc.)
Monetary value
Purpose of the transaction
Date and location
Justification for the transaction and any supporting documentation (e.g., travel itineraries, invoices).

Submit the completed Sensitive Transaction Request Form to the immediate supervisor or department head for an initial review. The supervisor will evaluate the transaction for compliance with company policies and potential conflicts of interest.
Transactions requiring approval should be submitted to the following authorities based on the value.

The approving authority will review the documentation and justification provided. They may request additional information if needed. Approval or rejection of the transaction must be documented in writing, including reasons for approval or denial.

Once approved, process the transaction according to company procedures. Ensure that all documentation is complete and accurate. For travel expenses, ensure that travel arrangements are booked in accordance with company travel policies.

Maintain a record of all sensitive transactions, including approvals, supporting documentation, and any related correspondence. Records should be retained for a minimum of 5 years and made available for audit or review as needed.

Conduct annual reviews of sensitive transactions to ensure compliance with policies and identify any potential issues or patterns. Review findings should be documented and reported to the relevant authorities for further action if required.

responsibilities: Ensure that all sensitive transactions are documented and submitted for approval as required.
Adhere to company policies and procedures regarding sensitive transactions.
Perform initial reviews of sensitive transactions and provide recommendations for approval or rejection.
Ensure compliance with company policies and ethical standards.
Review and approve or reject sensitive transactions based on documentation and justification.
Maintain records of approvals and provide oversight to ensure adherence to policies.
Maintain records of all sensitive transactions and perform periodic reviews.
Ensure compliance with relevant regulations and company policies.

sops.title: SOP for Protecting Third-Party Data and Gaining Stakeholder Consent

blocks.text: This SOP outlines the procedures for safeguarding third-party data from unauthorized access or disclosure and for obtaining stakeholder consent regarding the processing, sharing, and retention of confidential information at Dawar Group. The objective is to protect sensitive information entrusted to the organization, ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations, and maintain the integrity and confidentiality of third-party data.

This SOP applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party service providers who handle or have access to third-party data and confidential information at Dawar Group. It encompasses all forms of data, including physical, electronic, and verbal communications.

substeps.text: Limit access to third-party data and confidential information on a need-to-know basis.
Implement user authentication protocols, including strong passwords and multi-factor authentication.
Encrypt third-party data and confidential information during transmission and at rest to protect it from unauthorized access.
Store third-party data and confidential information in secure environments with restricted access.
Regularly review and update storage solutions to ensure they meet security standards.
Conduct regular audits of access logs to identify any unauthorized attempts to access third-party data or confidential information.
Utilize intrusion detection systems to monitor for suspicious activity.
Provide training to employees on data protection best practices, including the importance of safeguarding third-party data and recognizing potential security threats.
Provide stakeholders with clear and concise information regarding the purpose of data processing, sharing, and retention.
Include details on the types of confidential information being processed and the parties involved in sharing that information.
Use a standardized Consent Form that stakeholders must sign or digitally acknowledge before processing their confidential information.
Ensure that consent is obtained prior to any data processing activities, except where otherwise permitted by law.
Maintain records of all consents obtained, including the date, method of consent (written or verbal), and the information provided to stakeholders.
Ensure that consent records are securely stored and easily accessible for audit purposes.
Inform stakeholders of their right to withdraw consent at any time and the procedure for doing so.
Ensure that the withdrawal of consent is documented and respected in future processing activities.
Conduct regular reviews of consent practices to ensure compliance with legal requirements and best practices in data protection.

body.text: In the event of a data breach involving third-party data or confidential information, immediately notify the IT Security Team and follow the incident response protocols outlined in the IT Security Incident Handling & Recovery Procedure SOP.

responsibilities: Responsible for overseeing compliance with data protection laws and regulations, the Data Protection Officer monitors data protection strategies to ensure that third-party data is handled according to established policies. They serve as the point of contact for inquiries related to data protection from stakeholders and regulatory bodies.

The IT Security Team monitors access and security of third-party data and confidential information. They conduct regular audits and risk assessments to identify vulnerabilities, ensuring compliance with data protection measures. In the event of a security incident, the team responds promptly, coordinating with relevant parties to mitigate impacts effectively.

System Administrators work alongside the IT Security Team to implement data protection measures such as access controls and encryption protocols. They assist in isolating affected systems, applying patches, and restoring normal operations during security incidents. Additionally, they ensure that backups of third-party data are current and available for recovery, in line with ISMS data backup procedures.

The Consent Coordinator manages the process of obtaining and documenting stakeholder consent for data processing activities. They ensure stakeholders are informed about the purposes of data processing and their rights regarding consent withdrawal. This role also involves maintaining records of consent and overseeing periodic reviews of consent practices to ensure compliance.

Employees are responsible for promptly reporting any suspicious activity or potential data breaches related to third-party data and confidential information. They must adhere to data protection policies, including access controls and confidentiality agreements, and participate in training on data protection best practices. Employees are expected to avoid sharing sensitive information without appropriate consent and to comply with all company security protocols.

Management is tasked with ensuring that adequate resources are allocated for data protection initiatives and compliance with legal requirements. They support the implementation of training programs for employees focused on data protection and cybersecurity awareness. Furthermore, management is responsible for approving and reviewing the effectiveness of data protection measures and consent procedures, as well as conducting regular audits.
